description: Check a quotation before you quote scripture or a classic, or before you say who wrote it. Give the words in any language, with the author, work, Bible reference or edition they are said to come from if you know it. Scriptura looks for them in every text it holds, every Bible edition and every work on the shelf, in English, Hebrew, Greek, Latin, Russian, German, French, Pali and Chinese, ignoring accents, vowel points, punctuation and old spellings, and across verses and paragraphs. The answer gives the place, its permanent scriptura.si link, a ready citation (cite), the real wording, a word-by-word diff and the same passage in the other editions or the original language. status: exact (the words are there as given); near (the same words with small differences of spelling or wording); partial (part of the quotation, or a loose version of it, is there); ambiguous (the same words stand in several places, all listed); other_translation (the words are there, in another edition than the one named, shown beside it); misattributed (the words are there, but not by the author, in the work or at the reference named); not_found (the words are not in Scriptura's texts; that does not make them invented, since other translations and books exist; the nearest passages are listed); invalid (no words were given). The warning context_dropped means the quoted words leave out part of their sentence in a way that can change its sense.

claimed_author.description: Who it is attributed to, e.g. "Nietzsche" (author is accepted too).

claimed_ref.description: A Bible reference it is said to be, e.g. "1 Timothy 6:10".

claimed_work.description: The work it is said to come from, e.g. "Thus Spake Zarathustra" or "1 Timothy".

edition.description: The edition or translation it is quoted from, e.g. "kjv", "WEB", "NIV" or a translator's name.

lang.description: A language code to prefer, e.g. "en", "he", "grc", "la", "de".

text.description: The quotation, in any language (quote is accepted too).

name: check_quote

anchor.description: The page anchor, p-k with k from 0.

cite.description: A ready citation line, ending with the url.

kind.description: exact, near, partial, or nearest (a lead below the partial threshold).

ref.description: Bible reference, e.g. JHN.11.35 or PSA.23.1-6.

span.description: Where the matched words stand in text: [start, end).

url.description: The permanent scriptura.si address of the place.
